I just got back from depositing my partner Pokémon
in the PC at the Pokémon Center.

We spent every day together. Being separated like
this is so hard. But I know we’ll meet again someday.
I’m sure of it.

I’ll need to evacuate with the others pretty soon, but
first I’m planning to go take one last look at all the
cities my partner and I visited together.
It’s hard to explain why, but I feel the need to do this.

I remember this being a bright, bustling port city
way back when I visited with my partner.

Now there are always dark clouds looming over the
city. Not a single sunbeam slips through. Looks like
most of the people who lived here have gone, too.

The last time we were here, whenever we went near
the water, got so nervous...

Maybe because it can’t swim?

I tried getting it to transform into a Water type,
but despite its best efforts, we had little success.
I guess it’s not so easy.

After giving it a lot of encouragement, I was shocked
when it suddenly transformed into ME!

It copied every detail of my clothes, my haircut...
Only its face still looked like Ditto. Unfortunately,
transforming into me didn’t really help with the whole
“not being able to swim” issue...

A long time ago, this city was packed with people
working in the nearby mines. Apparently, it was a
pretty lively place.

At least, that’s what I heard from the chef at the little
restaurant I visited with .

There’s no sign of that restaurant anymore. But I
guess it’s not surprising, given those vicious volcanic
eruptions. Who could live in a place like this now?

The food we had at that restaurant was incredibly
delicious. The whole time the chef was cooking,
was watching intently.

It’s always been so full of curiosity. I’ve noticed it
seems particularly interested in the things humans do.

I wish we could have traveled together more. There
are so many things I wanted to show it.

This city was a dazzling metropolis the last time I
came here with .

Now it’s barely recognizable.

Apparently, the ground in this area has been rising up
so quickly that it’s caused many of the buildings to
collapse and the roads to crack.

Some scientists believe that if things continue at this
pace, in a matter of centuries this area will be...

...as high as a mountain, in terms of elevation. It looks
like most of the people who once lived here have
evacuated already.

I suppose I should go, too. It breaks my heart to leave
behind, but it’s not forever.

No matter what, I’ll come back someday. And then
and I will travel the world!

On June 11, I saved a Wimpod that was being chased
by a wild Meowth on this bridge.
It was wearing a light-blue ribbon, which makes me
think it has a Trainer.
If anyone knows who this Wimpod belongs to, please
contact me!

Seasonal Drink Menu Ideas
- Smoothie: Definite yes
- Watermelon and Soda Pop base: Definite yes
- Want something really original for our shop
- Maybe add berries?
Leppa Berry: Turned out a little bland
Chesto Berry: Hard to pair with watermelon
Aspear Berry: Refreshing—this might be the one!

There were many hardships to overcome, but we
finally made it back to this planet.

However, the environmental degradation is
proceeding at a much quicker rate than we imagined.
I doubt we’ll be able to stay for long.

I was originally slated to help survey the Fuchsia City
area. I thought it would be an excellent opportunity
to search for my lost Tangela, but...

we discovered the Cerulean City area has a high
chance of sinking into the ocean in the near future.
Therefore, we made the decision to prioritize
surveying here instead.

Considering our current energy crisis, I do not know
when we will be able to return to this planet.

But I have not given up hope.

On the space station we evacuated to, many of the
younger individuals I’ve met believe there will come a
day when we can once again live on this planet with
our Pokémon.

We must persist in our efforts—not only for our own
sake but also for that hopeful younger generation.

Experts in a wide range of fields from all over the
world have joined the survey team.

We quickly discovered that the eldest is a renowned
Pokémon Professor from Fuchsia City. Even so, he has
no air of superiority, and he interacts with the
younger researchers as if we’re all friends and
coworkers on the same level.

We started calling him simply “The Professor” to
show our respect for him.

The Professor caught a cold yesterday.

When I went to check on him, I found he had brought
a large amount of research materials and reports to
his bed and had been poring over them.

I suggested that he relax more given his condition,
but he laughed and said, “I’m still alive, and as long
as I have a working brain, I’d be a fool not to use it!”

This situation humanity has found itself in...

has no easy solution. That is without a doubt. And
yet, as I spend more time with The Professor, I find
myself feeling strangely optimistic.

As long as we remain steadfast in our efforts, I feel
there will certainly come a day when we can once
again live here on this planet with Pokémon.
